sections.heading: a b s t r a c t
sections.text:
Energy consumption of electronic devices continues to reduce dramatically, enabling the ambient energy harvesting devices as a solution for powering the wireless sensor nodes (WSNs), micro-electromechanical systems and portable electronics. Over the years, vibration-based piezoelectric harvesting has been emerged as a potential technology to recharge/replace chemical batteries in WSNs. A conventional linear piezoelectric energy harvester (PEH) cannot meet the requirement of broadband vibration resources as it generates useful power only in a narrow bandwidth near the resonant frequency. Several techniques such as passive/active resonance tuning, array of harvester beams, nonlinear designs and multi-degree-of-freedom energy harvesters have been investigated. This paper proposes a generalized multi-mode PEH (MPEH) accompanied with analytical modeling, which generates multiple close peaks of voltage output from low amplitude broadband and low frequency ambient vibration sources. The proposed MPEH comprises of a main cantilevered beam bonded with a patch of piezoelectric layer and attached with multiple branches with tip masses at their free ends. The useful bandwidth and the number of peaks for the MPEH could be tuned conveniently by varying multiple branches and tip masses. The proposed MPEH offers high design flexibility in tuning geometric parameters for achieving target frequencies and generates high power density. The mathematical modeling of generalized MPEH under transverse harmonic base vibrations is presented and the dynamic equations of the multi-modal harvester system are obtained following the Lagrangian method. The derived distributed parametric model of MPEH is more accurate than lumped parametric models of PEHS presented in the literature. The accuracy of the proposed analytical model is validated by two examples with numerical simulation and experimental results. It is shown that the multi-mode PEH has potential to generate sufficient power output from broadband vibration sources to sustain low-power electronic devices.

sections.heading: 1. Introduction
sections.text:
With the advancement in integrated circuitry and micro-electromechanical systems technology, energy consumption of recent electronics continues to reduce dramatically, encouraging ambient energy harvesting devices as an alternative for powering the portable electronics and wireless sensors. There are a variety of ambient sources available including solar, acoustic noise, temperature gradient and vibration for energy harvesting [1]. Ambient vibration sources are characterized by wide-band high energy density [1]. Vibration energy harvesting using piezoelectric transduction has advantages such as high energy density, high voltage output and ease of application over other vibration-to-electricity transduction mechanisms [2,3]. Over the last decade, there has been an explosion of research for the practical implementation of vibration-based piezoelectric harvesting technology [4–9].

A conventional linear piezoelectric energy harvester (LPEH) [10,11] comprises of a cantilevered beam as substrate with a lumped mass at the free end and a layer of piezoelectric layer bonded on the substrate structure fully or partially. However, this conventional LPEH generates useful power output in a narrow bandwidth near the resonant frequency. The power output of harvester decreases drastically when the excitation frequency of vibration source slightly varies from the natural frequency of harvester. Thus, the conventional LPEH is not suitable for the case that the natural frequency of the harvester does not match with the excitation frequency of ambient vibration source, or the bandwidth of the harvester cannot cover the wideband frequency spectrum of external sources. Many designs of harvesters with different techniques have been researched to improve the bandwidth of the conventional LPEH for the practical implementation of vibration energy harvester.

Array of conventional LPEH with multiple resonant frequencies has been presented to improve the power output performance for energy harvester. Shahruz [12,13] studied a mechanical band-pass filter for the purpose of energy scavenging. The dimensions of beams and tip masses can be tuned, so that assembly of such systems would act as a band-pass filter in a certain frequency band. Liu et al. [14] designed and fabricated a piezoelectric cantilevered array to improve power output and widen bandwidth. The resonances of cantilevered array cab be matched to the bandwidth of excited frequency of lowamplitude ambient vibration. Xue et al. [15] designed an ensemble of piezoelectric bimorphs with different resonant frequencies and found that the operation frequency of the harvester could be matched to the dominant frequency band of the ambient vibration source. Lin et al. [16] investigated the response of harvesters connected in series and integrated with various interface electronics including standard and parallel and series synchronized switch harvesting on inductor circuits. Upadrashta and Yang [17] proposed a nonlinear harvester array for energy harvesting from wideband, low-frequency and low-amplitude vibration sources. The proposed system uses combination of attractive and repulsive piezo-magnetoelastic harvesters for achieving wideband operation.

The fundamental mode of cantilever-type PEH is predominantly utilized in the literature for ambient vibration energy harvesting. The higher modes of harvester are ineffectual for energy harvesting since they are greatly separated from the first-order mode. Some multiple-degree-of-freedom (DOF) PEHs have been presented to achieve multi-peak voltage or power output. Erturk et al. [18] proposed a L-shaped PEH and tuned the two natural frequencies close to each other to achieve broadband energy harvesting. Kim et al. [19] proposed a 2-DOF PEH comprised of two cantilevered beams connected by a proof mass. Tang and Yang [20] proposed a multiple-DOF PEH including a 2-DOF model and a generalized n-DOF model. An equivalent circuit model of the generalized n-DOF harvester was developed using the analogy between the electrical and mechanical domains. Berdy et al. [21] proposed a wide bandwidth, meandering PEH by using the sensor node electronics as a distributed inertial mass. The wide bandwidth was resulted from the distributed inertial mass in combination with the meandering harvester’s close natural frequency spacing. Wu et al. [22,23] proposed a 2-DOF PEH composed of a main cantilevered beam and a secondary cantilevered beam cut out within the main beam. The two resonant frequencies were adjusted to be close by changing the proof masses to generate a wide bandwidth for energy harvesting. Zhang and Hu [24] utilized a branched beam system to maximize the performance of the harvesting device. The system comprised of one main cantilevered beam with a piezoelectric layer and a tip mass at the free end and several branched beams with proof masses at their free ends to increase the number of voltage output peaks of the harvester. Xiao et al. [25] presented that the performance of vibration energy harvesting system could be improved by introducing some piezoelectric elements among oscillators. Yang et al. [26] presented a hybrid nonlinear PEH combining bi-stability with internal resonance to increase the bandwidth. Wang and Tang [27] proposed a bistable 2-DOF PEH with a parasitic oscillator and magnet. Sun and Peter [28] proposed a horizontal asymmetric U-shaped PEH to generate two resonant peaks. Fu and Yeatman [29] presented a theoretical modelling of a rotational harvester with bi-stable configuration for harvesting low-frequency kinetic energy of wide bandwidth. Aridogan et al. [30] presented theoretical modeling and experimental results of a piezoelectric harvester integrated with a thin plate. Power generation performance from multiple vibration modes was investigated analytically and experimentally. Later, they [31] derived closed-form solutions of displacement and voltage responses for multiple vibration modes of a fully clamped thin plate for both series and parallel connections. Hu and Xu [32] presented a wideband multimass multi-spring PEH based on a folded asymmetric gapped cantilever, generating multiple resonant modes. Mehdipour et al. [33] proposed a S-Shaped design to harvest energy from several modes of the harvester.

Although many designs have been published using various techniques, obtaining multiple peaks in the dynamic response of harvester with useful power output for achieving broadband vibration energy harvesting remains as a challenge. Many of the above described works used either large tip masses or arrays of cantilevered beams resulting in reduction of power density. The high-order resonances of PEH away from the first resonance are usually ignored because the high frequency generates lower amplitude level when compared with the fundamental resonance. Thus, it is significant to obtain multiple close peaks to harvester wideband vibration energies. In this work, a generalized multi-mode piezoelectric energy harvester (MPEH) is proposed to obtain multiple close peaks of voltage output. The generalized MPEH comprises of a main cantilevered beam with a patch of piezoelectric layer and multiple branches with tip masses at their free ends. The proposed MPEH offers high design flexibility in tuning the geometric parameters for achieving target frequencies and generates high power density when compared with other multimodal harvesters. A generalized distributed parametric model of MPEH is derived and validated, which is more accurate than lumped parametric model presented in literature. The proposed model will be helpful in designing the MPEH for a target frequency range and facilitates quick parametric study.

The content of the paper is organized as follows: The mathematical formulation of MPEH under harmonic base excitation is derived in Section 2. Firstly, the fundamental mathematical model of the MPEH is established, and the formulations of electrical and mechanical energies are given and discretized by multiple mode shape functions. Secondly, the coupled electro-mechanical dynamic equations of harvester system are derived using the Lagrangian principle. Lastly, the voltage output response of harvester under harmonic excitation is obtained. In Section 3, the accuracy of developed analytical model is validated by numerical simulation and experimental results using two MPEH design examples. In Section 4, the analytical model is used for analyzing and optimizing the natural frequencies of the MPEH. Section 5 presents the conclusions of the paper.

This paper presents the analytical modeling of generalized MPEH. The schematic of generalized multi-mode harvester along with geometric parameters is shown in Fig. 1. The MPEH comprises of a main beam (or substrate) with a patch of piezoelectric layer bonded on it. Multiple branches (or affiliated beams) with tip masses are attached to the free end of the main beam. The length and width of the main beam are $L _ { 0 }$ and $b _ { s } ,$ respectively. The length and width of the piezoelectric layer are $L _ { p }$ and $b _ { p }$ , respectively. The thicknesses of main beam and piezoelectric layer are $d _ { s }$ and $d _ { p } ,$ , respectively. Without loss of generality, the piezoelectric layer is covered over the main beam at an arbitrary location such as between $x = L _ { p 1 }$ and $x = L _ { p 2 } \left( L _ { p } = L _ { p 2 } - L _ { p 1 } \right)$ . A tip mass $\left( M _ { t 0 } \right)$ with moment of inertia $I _ { t 0 }$ is assumed to be attached to the end of main beam. The material properties including the Young’s modulus and mass density of the main beam and the piezoelectric layer are $E _ { s } , \rho _ { s } , E _ { p } , \rho _ { p }$ , respectively. The subscripts of s and $p$ stand for the main substrate beam and piezoelectric layer, respectively. For each branch, the geometrical dimensions are $L _ { k , } b _ { k } , d _ { k }$ and the properties are $E _ { k } , \rho _ { k }$ , respectively $k = 1 , 2 , . . . \ : K$ , where K is the number of the branches).

sections.heading: 3.2. Validation case 2: MPEH with four branches
sections.text:
In this section another design of MPEH with four branches is studied and the detailed dimensions of the MPEH are shown in Fig. 7. The thickness of the main beam and branches is $1 \mathrm { m m }$ and $0 . 5 \mathrm { m m }$ , respectively. The main beam and branches of the MPEH are made of aluminum. The same MFC is bonded on the main beam. The material properties of MPEH are given in Table 1. In order to further validate the accuracy of the analytical model, finite element simulations are implemented in commercial software ANSYS 17.0. Few researchers have used finite element modeling for analyzing the dynamics of complex piezoelectric harvesters and for validating the analytical models of linear and nonlinear piezoelectric energy harvesters [39,40]. The details of 3-D finite element modeling of the MPEH with four branches is presented in Fig. 8. The main beam and branches are meshed with 3-dimensional 20-node brick elements (SOLID186) which have three translational DOFs at each node in orthogonal directions. MFC patch bonded on the main beam is meshed with 3-dimensional 20-node coupled-field piezoelectric element (SOLID226) having additional supplementary DOF of voltage for each node along with the three translational DOFs. A linear resistor element (CIRCU94) is connected across the MFC to measure the electrical output under harmonic base excitation. The voltage output at one node of the resistor element is set to zero (grounded) and the voltage generated from the harvester is thus obtained at the other node. The resistance is set to $1 \ \mathsf { M } \Omega$ to simulate the open circuit condition. The simulation model has a total of 2735 elements. sections.heading: 5. Conclusion
sections.text: The paper presents a generalized multi-mode piezoelectric energy harvester and its analytical modeling. The novel MPEH generates multiple close peaks of voltage output from broadband and low frequency ambient vibration sources. The bandwidth and the number of peaks of the harvester can be tuned conveniently by varying the number of branches, dimensions of the beams and tip masses. Furthermore, the proposed MPEH gives better design flexibility in tuning geometric parameters for achieving target frequencies and achieves higher power density compared to other multi-modal harvesters. The mathematical model of the MPEH is formulated, and the electromechanical equations are obtained by applying the Lagrangian equations. The accuracy of the proposed analytical modeling is validated by finite element simulation and experiments. The derived distributed parametric analytical model of MPEH taking more mode shapes is more accurate than lumped parametric model presented in literature. Two harvester designs are chosen for validation, one with three branches and the other with four branches. The comparison shows very good agreement validating the accuracy of the proposed analytical model multi-mode harvesters. The proposed analytical model is useful in designing the multi-mode harvesters for a target frequency range and facilitates rapid parametric studies. It is also demonstrated that the proposed MPEH generates higher normalized power or normalized power density at respective resonances when compared with other multimodal designs. The proposed MPEH has advantages over nonlinear harvesters for low-amplitude broadband vibration sources. It thus has potential to harvest adequate energy from ambient broadband vibration sources to power wireless sensors, microelectromechanical systems and portable electronics.
